DataVivid 0.1.4 adds a chart panel: a quick chart of the columns you select.

## Charts

The new panel under the grid charts the selected column. If you select a range of columns, it charts the first against the last. You can also pick X and Y by hand. The chart type follows the column types, so there is nothing to set up:

| You select | You get |
|---|---|
| a number column | a histogram (one bar per value for small whole-number ranges) |
| a text, category or yes/no column | rows per value: the top 24, the rest as *Other*, missing values as their own bar |
| a date column | rows per day, week, month, quarter or year (picked automatically, or choose one) |
| two number columns | a scatter plot with the correlation; tables with more than 50,000 rows show a random sample of 50,000 points |
| a text and a number column | the mean, sum, median, minimum, maximum or row count per category, or box plots of the spread |
| a date and a number column | a line of that value per period |

- **Click a bar** to keep only the rows with that value. Like every other filter, it is a step in the *Steps* list, so you can undo it.
- **Copy data** copies the numbers behind the chart as a table that pastes into Excel.
- Charts are computed in the background and only the totals are drawn, so a chart of a million rows appears in a moment.
- Hide the panel with *Hide*, or show it again with *View > Chart panel*.

## Fixes

- Applying a filter that removes no rows no longer adds an empty step.

## Install

**Windows 10/11 (x64):** run `DataVivid-0.1.4-windows-x64-setup.exe`. It replaces an older DataVivid. The zip and the portable `datavivid.exe` are still available.

**Linux (x64, glibc 2.35+: Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+, Fedora 36+)**

```bash
tar xzf DataVivid-0.1.4-linux-x64.tar.gz
cd DataVivid-0.1.4-linux-x64
./install.sh                 # or ./install.sh --no-default
```
